issues.legal_issue: A bank cannot accept a unilateral pledge of a jointly owned fixed deposit or apply it to the debt of one account holder when the other account holder has not consented.
material_facts: The fixed deposit was jointly held by the appellant and her husband and was payable to either holder or the survivor.
The bank applied the deposit to a loan owed by a borrower and his business; the appellant was not liable for that loan.
The appellant had not authorized or consented to the pledge or adjustment, and the court found no independent finding by the lower fora that her husband had in fact pledged the receipt.
The bank refused to pay the appellant her share of the deposit.
issues.conclusion: The bank had no right to apply the joint deposit to the debt without the appellant’s consent. Its refusal to pay her was contrary to banking norms and constituted deficient service; the consumer complaint was properly allowed.
issues.legal_principle: An either-or-survivor term permits the bank to discharge its debt by paying either account holder at maturity; it does not authorize one holder to alter the joint deposit contract unilaterally by pledging the deposit. The bank’s debt is owed to the joint holders, not to the debtor-holder alone, and cannot be set off against that holder’s separate debt. The Court approved Simla Banking and Industrial Company Ltd. v. Mt. Bhagwan Kaur, AIR 1928 Lahore 316, followed in Nath Bank Ltd. v. Sisir Kumar Sarkar, AIR 1954 Cal. 303, and relied on Hirschorn v. Evans (Barclays Bank Ltd., Garnishees), 1938 (2) KB 801. Punjab National Bank v. Surendra Prasad Sinha, 1993 (1) SCC 499, was distinguishable because both account holders there guaranteed the debt and jointly provided the deposit as security.

rule.if: consumer_appeal_about_refusal_to_pay_joint_deposit and deposit_jointly_owned and either_or_survivor_payment_term and deposit_applied_to_one_holders_separate_debt and other_holder_did_not_consent

predicates.consumer_appeal_about_refusal_to_pay_joi: A consumer appeal concerns a bank’s refusal to pay money held in a jointly owned deposit.
predicates.deposit_jointly_owned: The deposit was held in the names of more than one account holder.
predicates.either_or_survivor_payment_term: The deposit terms allowed payment at maturity to either holder or the survivor.
predicates.deposit_applied_to_one_holders_separate_: The bank applied the joint deposit to a debt for which only one of the holders was liable.
predicates.other_holder_did_not_consent: The other joint holder did not authorize or consent to the pledge or application of the deposit.

issues.definition: When a consumer appeal concerns an unpaid joint deposit with an either-or-survivor payment term, and the bank applied it to one holder’s separate debt without the other holder’s consent, the bank cannot make that application and its refusal to pay is deficient service.

issues.legal_issue: An order in a loan proceeding does not bind a joint deposit holder who was not a party to that proceeding or establish that the holder’s interest in the deposit was pledged.
material_facts: The bank’s loan suit did not include the appellant as a party.
The bank applied to the court hearing that suit to report that the fixed deposit had been given as security and had been applied to the loan.
The trial court allowed the bank’s application, but the revisional court held that the order did not bind the appellant and that the deposit dispute was not an issue in the suit.

The consumer commissions treated the civil-court proceedings as establishing that the deposit had been pledged, although the Supreme Court found no independent finding by any forum that the pledge had been created.
issues.conclusion: The trial-court order did not bind the appellant, and the consumer commissions erred in treating the civil-court proceedings as establishing that the deposit had been pledged.
issues.legal_principle: A determination in a proceeding does not resolve the rights of a person who was not a party where that person’s separate interest was not in issue. The Court agreed with the revisional court that the trial-court order did not bind the appellant; it did not decide whether that order was otherwise valid.

predicates.holder_not_party_to_prior_proceeding: The person whose interest in the deposit is affected was not a party to the earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_proceeding_did_not_put_holders_dep: The earlier proceeding did not place that person’s rights in the joint deposit in issue.
predicates.later_decision_relies_on_prior_order_as_: A later decision treats an order in the earlier proceeding as proof that the deposit was pledged.

issues.definition: When a person was not a party to an earlier proceeding, that proceeding did not put the person’s deposit rights in issue, and a later decision relies on its order as proof of a pledge, the order does not bind the person or establish a pledge of that person’s interest.
